From 41e76c85660c022c6bf5713bfb6c21e64a487cec Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jan Kara <jack@suse.cz>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2020 16:16:16 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] bfq: Avoid false bfq queue merging

bfq_setup_cooperator() uses bfqd->in_serv_last_pos so detect whether it
makes sense to merge current bfq queue with the in-service queue.
However if the in-service queue is freshly scheduled and didn't dispatch
any requests yet, bfqd->in_serv_last_pos is stale and contains value
from the previously scheduled bfq queue which can thus result in a bogus
decision that the two queues should be merged. This bug can be observed
for example with the following fio jobfile:

[global]
direct=0
ioengine=sync
invalidate=1
size=1g
rw=read

[reader]
numjobs=4
directory=/mnt

where the 4 processes will end up in the one shared bfq queue although
they do IO to physically very distant files (for some reason I was able to
observe this only with slice_idle=1ms setting).

Fix the problem by invalidating bfqd->in_serv_last_pos when switching
in-service queue.

Fixes: 058fdecc6de7 ("block, bfq: fix in-service-queue check for queue merging")
CC: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Jan Kara <jack@suse.cz>
Acked-by: Paolo Valente <paolo.valente@linaro.org>
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>

diff --git a/block/bfq-iosched.c b/block/bfq-iosched.c
index 23e293d2943c..4157cfe99ae2 100644
--- a/block/bfq-iosched.c
+++ b/block/bfq-iosched.c
@@ -3007,6 +3007,7 @@ static void __bfq_set_in_service_queue(struct bfq_data *bfqd,
 	}
 
 	bfqd->in_service_queue = bfqq;
+	bfqd->in_serv_last_pos = 0;
 }
 
 /*
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `block/bfq-iosched.c`**
   - A new line was added in the function `__bfq_set_in_service_queue` to set `bfqd->in_serv_last_pos` to `0` when switching the in-service queue. This change ensures that the last position of the in-service queue is reset, preventing the use of stale data that could lead to incorrect queue merging decisions.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in `block/bfq-iosched.c` addresses a bug related to the merging of BFQ (Budget Fair Queueing) queues. The issue arose because the `in_serv_last_pos` variable could contain outdated information when a new queue was scheduled, leading to incorrect merging of queues that should not be combined. By resetting `in_serv_last_pos` to `0` when a new queue is set as in-service, the patch ensures that the merging logic operates on valid data, thus preventing the false merging of queues that handle I/O requests for physically distant files. This fix is directly related to the previously identified bug in the queue merging logic, as noted in the patch description.

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs because the variable `bfqd->in_serv_last_pos` retains stale data from a previously scheduled BFQ queue when a new queue is set as in-service. This outdated value can lead to incorrect decisions about whether to merge the current queue with the in-service queue, resulting in queues that should not be combined being merged erroneously.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void __bfq_set_in_service_queue(struct bfq_data *bfqd,
 				       struct bfq_queue *bfqq)
 {
 	if (bfqq) {
 		bfq_clear_bfqq_fifo_expire(bfqq);
 
 		bfqd->budgets_assigned = (bfqd->budgets_assigned * 7 + 256) / 8;
 
 		if (time_is_before_jiffies(bfqq->last_wr_start_finish) &&
 		    bfqq->wr_coeff > 1 &&
 		    bfqq->wr_cur_max_time == bfqd->bfq_wr_rt_max_time &&
 		    time_is_before_jiffies(bfqq->budget_timeout)) {
 			/*
 			 * For soft real-time queues, move the start
 			 * of the weight-raising period forward by the
 			 * time the queue has not received any
 			 * service. Otherwise, a relatively long
 			 * service delay is likely to cause the
 			 * weight-raising period of the queue to end,
 			 * because of the short duration of the
 			 * weight-raising period of a soft real-time
 			 * queue.  It is worth noting that this move
 			 * is not so dangerous for the other queues,
 			 * because soft real-time queues are not
 			 * greedy.
 			 *
 			 * To not add a further variable, we use the
 			 * overloaded field budget_timeout to
 			 * determine for how long the queue has not
 			 * received service, i.e., how much time has
 			 * elapsed since the queue expired. However,
 			 * this is a little imprecise, because
 			 * budget_timeout is set to jiffies if bfqq
 			 * not only expires, but also remains with no
 			 * request.
 			 */
 			if (time_after(bfqq->budget_timeout,
 				       bfqq->last_wr_start_finish))
 				bfqq->last_wr_start_finish +=
 					jiffies - bfqq->budget_timeout;
 			else
 				bfqq->last_wr_start_finish = jiffies;
 		}
 
 		bfq_set_budget_timeout(bfqd, bfqq);
 		bfq_log_bfqq(bfqd, bfqq,
 			     "set_in_service_queue, cur-budget = %d",
 			     bfqq->entity.budget);
 	}
 
 	bfqd->in_service_queue = bfqq;
+	bfqd->in_serv_last_pos = 0;
 }
